newsitem.title: GERMANY: German copper plant worried over scrap supplies.
newsitem.headline: German copper plant worried over scrap supplies.

text.p: Leading European copper refiner Norddeutsche Affinerie (NA) said future scrap supplies to feed its integrated smelter were not secure because trade flows were turning away from Europe.
"Our cost structure makes it difficult for us to compete for scrap with companies in low cost countries," chairman Werner Marnette told a news conference on Wednesday.
"We are also unhappy about subsidisation and unfair tariff practices in some Southeast Asian countries and we plan to raise this issue at European Union level."
Scrap intake in the 1995/96 year to September 30 had fallen sharply to 84,000 tonnes from 113,000 a year earlier.
Scrap flows had slowed since the second half of 1996, when copper prices fell sharply from mid-year peaks, discouraging scrap merchant activity.
NA bought more blister copper from other producers and better ore supplies also helped it raise its cathodes output, which in 1995/96 was up six percent at 368,958 tonnes.
NA used 690,000 tonnes of ore concentrates in 1995/96 after 633,000 in 1994/95, and was confident it would secure enough ore in 1996/97 to maintain the same cathode output, Marnette said.
Global mine output was looking up but NA, which in earlier years had a two thirds/one third ratio of ore and scrap, would ideally like to be more flexible with its raw materials.
Attempts to secure domestic copper-bearing scrap in cooperation with electricity boards had not been very successful.
